academic_translation:
Because you will die very quickly,
You should gather the accumulations until then.
Even if you abandon laziness at that time,
What can you do when it is not the right time?
translation: You will die very quickly. Until then, you should gather stored-up goodness. Even if you give up laziness at the very end, what can you do when it is too late?

academic_translation:
"This is not done, this is just begun,
And this remains only half-done"—
When the Lord of Death suddenly arrives,
I will think, "Alas, I am destroyed!"
translation: I will think, "I haven't finished this. I just started that. This is only half done." Then the Lord of Death will suddenly arrive. I will think, "Oh no, I am ruined!"

academic_translation:
With eyes red and swollen by the force of grief,
Tears streaming down their faces,
My relatives having lost all hope,
I will gaze upon the faces of the messengers of Yama.
translation: My relatives will lose all hope. Their eyes will be red and puffy from crying. Tears will run down their faces. Then I will look into the faces of the messengers of Yama.

academic_translation:
Tormented by the memory of my own misdeeds,
And hearing the sounds of hell,
I will soil my body with filth in terror;
When I become delirious, what will I do?
translation: Remembering my own harmful deeds will torment me. I will hear the sounds of hell. I will be so terrified that I soil myself. When my mind gets confused, what will I do?

academic_translation:
If you, like a live fish writhing about,
Are possessed by fear in this life,
Having committed misdeeds, what need is there to mention
The unbearable sufferings of hell?
translation: In this life, you flip around in fear like a live fish out of water. Since you have done harmful deeds, there is no need to mention the unbearable sufferings of hell!

academic_translation:
When touched by hot water,
You of tender flesh are intensely scorched;
Having created the karma of hell,
Why do you remain at ease like this?
translation: When hot water touches you, your soft skin burns badly. You have done actions that lead to hell. Why are you just relaxing like this?

academic_translation:
Desiring the result without exertion,
Being fragile and subject to many harms,
Seized by death, yet acting like a god—
Alas, you are destroyed by sufferings!
translation: You want the result without trying hard. You are fragile and face many harms. Death is grabbing you, yet you act like a god. Oh no, you are destroyed by sufferings!

academic_translation:
Relying on the boat of a human body,
Cross over the great river of suffering!
Since this boat will be hard to find later,
O fool, do not sleep at this time!
translation: Use the boat of a human body to cross the great river of suffering! This boat will be hard to find later. So do not be foolish and sleep right now!

academic_translation:
Having abandoned the supreme joy of the sublime Dharma,
Which is a boundless cause of joy,
Why do you delight in distraction by the causes of suffering,
And in agitation and the like?
translation: The holy teachings are an endless cause of joy. Why have you left their great joy behind? Why do you enjoy distraction by the causes of suffering, along with restlessness and the like?

academic_translation:
Without despondency, with a host of forces,
With earnest application and self-mastery,
Practice the equality of self and others,
And the exchange of self and others!

locked_terms.use: seeing self and others as equal

translation: Let go of discouragement. Gather your force with wholehearted commitment and mastery of oneself. Practice seeing self and others as equal! Practice swapping self and others!

academic_translation:
Thinking, "How could I attain awakening?"
Do not fall into despondency;
For in this way the Tathāgata,
The Speaker of Truth, has spoken this truth:
translation: Do not fall into discouragement by thinking, "How could I ever reach awakening?" The Thus-Gone One is the Speaker of Truth, and he has spoken this truth:

academic_translation:
Flies, gadflies, and bees,
And likewise whatever has become a worm—
Even they, if they generate the power of diligence,
Will attain unsurpassable awakening, which is hard to attain.
translation: Think of flies, mosquitoes, bees, and worms. Even they can build up the power of joyful effort. If they do, they will reach the highest awakening, which is very hard to achieve.

academic_translation:
Since someone like me has been born as a human by birth,
And recognizes what is beneficial and harmful,
If I do not abandon the conduct of awakening,
Why should I not attain awakening?
translation: I have been born as a human being. I know what is helpful and what is harmful. If I do not give up the way of acting for awakening, why should I not reach awakening?

academic_translation:
"But my arms, legs, and so forth,
Must be given away, so I am afraid," if I think—
Without analyzing what is heavy and what is light,
I am merely afraid due to delusion.
translation: I might think, "I am afraid to give away my arms and legs." But this fear is just confusion. I am not thinking about what is truly hard and what is easy.

academic_translation:
For countless tens of millions of eons,
I will be cut many times over,
Pierced, burned, and split apart,
Yet I will not attain awakening.
translation: For countless millions of great ages, I will be cut many times. I will be pierced, burned, and split apart. Even so, I will not reach awakening.

academic_translation:
The suffering of my accomplishing awakening
Has a limit;
It is just like the suffering of cutting open the body
In order to remove the harm of a splinter destroying it from within.
translation: The suffering of reaching awakening has a limit. It is just like the pain of cutting the body open. You do it to pull out a splinter that is destroying you from the inside.

academic_translation:
Even all physicians, through medical treatments,
Cure illness by means of discomfort;
Therefore, to destroy many sufferings,
I should endure a minor discomfort.
translation: All doctors cure sickness by causing some discomfort with their treatments. Therefore, to destroy many sufferings, I should put up with a little discomfort.

academic_translation:
Such ordinary medical treatments
The Supreme Physician does not perform;
Through an extremely gentle method,
He cures immeasurable great diseases.
translation: The Greatest Doctor does not use normal treatments like these. He uses a very gentle method. With it, he cures countless great diseases.

academic_translation:
Even in generosity with vegetables and so forth,
The Guide initially engages one;
Having become accustomed to that, later on,
One gradually gives away even one's own flesh.
translation: At first, the Guide starts us off with giving vegetables and things like that. Once we get used to that, we can slowly learn to give away even our own flesh.

academic_translation:
When, regarding one's own body,
An attitude arises that it is like vegetables and so forth,
At that time, in giving away flesh and so forth,
What difficulty is there in that?
translation: When I think of my own body as being like simple vegetables, giving away my flesh is no longer hard. What difficulty is there in that?

academic_translation:
Because of having abandoned misdeeds, there is no suffering;
Because of being a wise person, there is no unhappiness.
In this way, wrong conceptions
And misdeeds harm the mind and body.
translation: If I give up every harmful deed, I will have no suffering. If I am a wise person, I will not be unhappy. It is wrong thinking and harmful deeds that hurt the mind and body.

academic_translation:
If the body is at ease through merit,
And the mind is at ease through being a wise person,
Even while remaining in saṃsāra for the welfare of others,
Why would the compassionate ones become weary?
translation: A store of goodness puts the body at ease. Being a wise person puts the mind at ease. Even while staying in the cycle of rebirth for the good of others, why would a compassionate one get tired?

academic_translation:
Because this bodhisattva, through the power of bodhicitta,
Exhausts previous misdeeds
And gathers an ocean of merit,
He is explained to be superior to the Śrāvakas.
translation: The power of the awakening mind wipes out every past harmful deed. It also gathers an ocean of stored goodness. Because of this, the bodhisattva is greater than the Hearers.

academic_translation:
Therefore, having mounted the horse of bodhicitta,
Which dispels all weariness and fatigue,
While proceeding from happiness to happiness,
What intelligent person would fall into despondency?
translation: So climb onto the horse of the awakening mind! It takes away all tiredness. As you ride from happiness to happiness, what smart person would ever fall into discouragement?

academic_translation:
To accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, the forces
Are aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and relinquishment.
Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering
And by contemplating the benefits of that aspiration.
translation: To help living beings, we need four kinds of strength. These are a strong wish, steadiness, joy, and letting go. A strong wish grows from the fear of suffering and from thinking about the benefits of that wish.

academic_translation:
Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors,
Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment,
And the powers of earnest application and mastery,
I should strive to increase diligence.
translation: I must leave the opposite behind. I should try hard to grow my joyful effort. I will do this through a strong wish, pride, joy, and letting go. I will also use the power of wholehearted commitment and mastery.

academic_translation:
The faults of myself and others,
Which are immeasurable, I must destroy;
Wherein for each and every fault
An ocean of eons would be exhausted.
translation: I must destroy the countless faults of myself and others. It would take an ocean of great ages to end each and every fault.

academic_translation:
If of the effort to exhaust those faults,
I do not see even a fraction in myself,
Being an abode of immeasurable suffering,
Why does my heart not burst?
translation: I do not see even a tiny bit of effort in myself to end those faults. I am a place of endless suffering. Why does my heart not burst?

academic_translation:
The good qualities of myself and others,
Which are many, I must accomplish;
Wherein if for each and every good quality
I must familiarize myself for an ocean of eons,
translation: I must build up many good qualities in myself and others. I must practice each and every good quality for an ocean of great ages.

academic_translation:
I, for even a fraction of a good quality,
Have never generated familiarization;
Having somehow found this birth,
It is astonishing that I have made it meaningless.
translation: But I have never practiced even a tiny part of a good quality. I somehow found this life. It is amazing that I have made it meaningless.

academic_translation:
I have not made offerings to the Blessed One,
Nor provided the happiness of the great festival;
I have not performed service for the teaching,
Nor fulfilled the wishes of the poor.
translation: I have not made offerings to the Blessed One. I have not shared the joy of a great festival. I have not served the teachings. I have not fulfilled the wishes of the poor.

academic_translation:
If I have not given fearlessness to the frightened,
And have not given happiness to the distressed,
I have merely produced the pangs
And suffering of my mother's womb.
translation: If I have not given freedom from fear to frightened people, and I have not given happiness to sad people, then my birth only caused my mother pain and suffering.

academic_translation:
Because I have been devoid of aspiration for the Dharma,
Previously and even now,
Such destitution has come about;
Who would forsake aspiration for the Dharma?
translation: Because I did not have a strong wish for the teachings in the past, and still do not have it now, I have ended up so poor. Who would ever give up a strong wish for the teachings?

academic_translation:
The Sage has stated that aspiration
Is the root of all virtuous factors,
And its root constantly is
Meditating on the ripened result.
translation: The Sage has said that a strong wish is the root of every kind of good deed. The root of that strong wish is always meditating on the result that ripens.

academic_translation:
Suffering and mental unhappiness,
Various kinds of fears,
And separation from what is desired
Will arise from engaging in misdeeds.
translation: Suffering and unhappiness, many kinds of fears, and losing what we want all come from doing harmful deeds.

academic_translation:
By performing virtue intended in the mind,
Wherever one may go,
There, through that merit,
One will be manifestly honored with the offerings of its results.
translation: By doing a good deed planned in your mind, wherever you go, your store of goodness will bring you honor and the gifts of its results.

academic_translation:
Although those who commit misdeeds desire happiness,
Wherever they may go,
There, through those misdeeds,
They are completely destroyed by the weapons of suffering.
translation: People who do harmful deeds might want happiness. But wherever they go, those harmful deeds will destroy them with the weapons of suffering.

academic_translation:
Dwelling in the core of a vast, fragrant, and cool lotus,
With splendor nourished by the food of the Victor's sweet speech,
Possessing a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light,
Through virtue one becomes a son of the Sugata dwelling before the Victor.
translation: Because of my good deeds, I will become a child of the Well-Gone One. I will sit in front of the Victorious One. I will live inside a huge, cool, sweet-smelling lotus. The sweet words of the Victorious One will feed my bright glow. The light of the Sage will open my lotus, and I will have a perfect body.

academic_translation:
Utterly tormented by Yama's henchmen completely flaying one's skin,
Molten copper melted by intensely hot fire poured upon one's body,
Pierced by blazing swords and short spears, one's flesh scattered into a hundred pieces,
Through many non-virtues one falls onto the intensely blazing iron ground.
translation: By doing many bad deeds, I will fall onto the intensely burning iron ground. The helpers of Yama will cause me great pain by tearing off all my skin. They will pour melted, hot copper over my body. Blazing swords and short spears will pierce me, cutting my flesh into a hundred pieces.

academic_translation:
Therefore, one should aspire to virtue,
And cultivate it with reverence.
By the method of the Vajradhvaja,
Having begun, one should cultivate pride.
translation: Because of this, I should really want to do good deeds. I must practice them with great respect. Using the method of Vajradhvaja, once I begin, I should grow my pride.
